# Project Decisions — SustainIQ

Structured decision memory (spec §50–52). The source of truth is `.agylite/decisions.yaml`; record decisions with
`agylite decide add --kind <architecture|security|design|…> --topic … --decision … --reason …`.
The table below is regenerated between the markers; edit text outside them freely.

| D-016 | 2026-11-06 | architecture | OCR for scanned PDFs (demo) | Demo: tesseract.js in the upload Web Worker, self-hosted, only for text-less pages; Llama 3.2 Vision, OpenCV, PyMuPDF and Supabase pgvector not used | Measured on the owner's 4-page scan: tesseract 14-22 s, 97-98% of reference words; Llama 3.2 11B Vision 29-116 s per page and invented a repeating line on 1 of 4 pages; PyMuPDF is Python and AGPL; OpenCV adds ~10 MB for no gain on clean scans; pgvector's only gain (no index lag) is solved by keyword-first search | — | ACTIVE |
| D-017 | 2026-11-06 | security | Topic guard with uploads | When the owner has live uploads, the topic guard blocks only hazards and override attempts, not off-subject questions | A user's own PDF can be on any subject (the owner's test paper is on heart disease); answers still come only from the sources, so unrelated questions find nothing | — | ACTIVE |
| D-018 | 2026-11-06 | architecture | OCR in production (proposed) | Production: pdf.js for text PDFs; scanned pages via self-hosted PaddleOCR (if documents must stay in-house) or Google Document AI / Azure Read (~USD 1.50 per 1,000 pages); tesseract.js as fallback; background job via Cloudflare Queues/Workflows | Browser OCR is slow on phones and weaker on poor scans; to be benchmarked and decided with the client after the demos | — | ACTIVE |

| D-020 | 2026-11-06 | scope | No per-user upload limit | The 5 PDFs / 100 pages per user quota is removed; per-PDF caps (100 pages, 25 MB) and 7-day expiry stay | Owner: users must be able to upload as many PDFs as they need; the per-file caps protect the browser parser until server-side ingestion (P9) | — | ACTIVE |
| D-021 | 2026-11-15 | architecture | Hosting from the start | Production runs on Cloudflare Workers Paid (USD 5/month) with the owner's own domain on Cloudflare from day one; everything (app, D1, Vectorize, Workers AI, KV, R2, rate limits, Turnstile) stays on Cloudflare; Render retires once the move is done | Owner: everything on Cloudflare is simpler; Workers Paid removes the 10 ms CPU limit that forced Render (D-012); the domain unlocks DDoS, WAF, geo/IP firewall and cache rules | D-012 (for production) | ACTIVE |
| D-022 | 2026-11-15 | architecture | Any LLM provider | The answer model is a config choice: Groq, OpenAI (ChatGPT), Anthropic (Claude), Google (Gemini), Workers AI or others, each with its own key and URL, mixable in the fallback chain; provider-specific request fields come from config, not code | Owner: Groq is one option, not the plan; the cheapest model that passes the quality bar wins (T-9.11) | — | ACTIVE |

| D-024 | 2026-11-15 | security | Login method | Login is built into the app with a maintained auth library (e.g. Better Auth): own branded login page, invites and roles managed inside SustainIQ, no user cap; Cloudflare Access not used for user login | Owner chose the auth library over Cloudflare Access for control and no 50-user ceiling; the security rules in SECURITY §10 and T-11.8 apply | — | ACTIVE |
| D-025 | 2026-11-15 | scope | No pilot stage | The 5-user pilot stage is removed: after the audit and demo cleanup the plan goes straight to a full production launch, with no user cap and production-grade security, rate limits and scale from day one | Owner: protection level must be production from the start, not sized for a 5-user trial | — | ACTIVE |
| D-026 | 2026-11-15 | product | One login, roles in the app | One sign-in / sign-up page for every role (email + password or Google); roles admin, staff, user stored in our database; admins get an Admin section in the same app where they add and remove users and change roles; no separate admin login, no Cloudflare dashboard for user management | Owner: simplest for users and admins; everything managed in SustainIQ itself | — | ACTIVE |
| D-027 | 2026-11-15 | security | Allowed email domains | Sign-up and sign-in work only for allowed email domains (e.g. the college's .ac.in); public mail (Gmail, Hotmail, Yahoo…) is refused; the list lives in config, editable by an admin; the email must be verified (link for password accounts, email_verified for Google) | Owner: only college and professor addresses may use SustainIQ; verification stops someone typing a college address they don't own | — | ACTIVE |
| D-028 | 2026-11-15 | scope | No storage limit | The library has no upper size limit: 5–10 GB is only the starting size; design, costs and tests must hold as it grows (growth path in T-9.15) | Owner: uploads will keep growing past 10 GB | — | ACTIVE |
| D-029 | 2026-11-15 | architecture | Rented hosting, not the college's server | SustainIQ always runs on hosting we buy and run (Cloudflare first, D-021); the later college rollout scales that hosting instead of moving to a college server | Owner decision | — | ACTIVE |
